request.query: from unbounded set choose sequence of elements with prescribed successive growth

items.informal_name: Existence of Strictly Increasing Subsequence Satisfying Predicate Condition
items.type: ∀ {P : ℕ → Prop}, (∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ n, n > N ∧ P n) → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), P (φ n)
items.informal_description: For any predicate $ P : \mathbb{N} \to \text{Prop} $ such that for every $ N \in \mathbb{N} $, there exists an $ n > N $ with $ P(n) $, there exists a strictly increasing function $ \varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} $ such that $ P(\varphi(n)) $ holds for all $ n \in \mathbb{N} $.

items.informal_name: Strictly Increasing Subsequence in NoMaxOrder for Tendsto atTop
items.type:
∀ {β : Type u_4} [inst : LinearOrder β] [NoMaxOrder β] {u : ℕ → β},
  Filter.Tendsto u Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ StrictMono (u ∘ φ)
items.informal_description: In a linearly ordered set $\beta$ with no maximum element, every sequence $u : \mathbb{N} \to \beta$ that satisfies $\mathcal{F}_{\text{atTop}}$-tendsto $u$ atTop atTop has a strictly increasing subsequence $u \circ \varphi$ for some strictly increasing $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.

items.informal_name: Extraction of Strictly Increasing Function from Frequent Conditions
items.type: ∀ {P : ℕ → ℕ → Prop}, (∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, P n k) → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), P n (φ n)
items.informal_description: If for every natural number $ n $, the proposition $ P(n, k) $ holds frequently as $ k $ approaches infinity (i.e., for arbitrarily large $ k $), then there exists a strictly increasing function $ \varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} $ such that $ P(n, \varphi(n)) $ holds for all $ n \in \mathbb{N} $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Strictly Increasing Subsequence for Frequent Properties at Infinity
items.type: ∀ {P : ℕ → Prop}, (∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, P n) → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), P (φ n)
items.informal_description: If a property $ P(n) $ holds frequently in the filter at infinity on natural numbers (i.e., for arbitrarily large $ n $), then there exists a strictly increasing function $ \varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} $ such that $ P(\varphi(n)) $ holds for all $ n \in \mathbb{N} $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Strictly Increasing Sequence Satisfying Uniformly Eventually Condition
items.type: ∀ {P : ℕ → ℕ → Prop}, (∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ N, ∀ k ≥ N, P n k) → ∃ φ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), P n (φ n)
items.informal_description: If for every natural number $ n $ there exists $ N $ such that $ P(n, k) $ holds for all $ k \geq N $, then there exists a strictly increasing function $ \varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} $ such that $ P(n, \varphi(n)) $ holds for all $ n $. This guarantees the existence of a strictly monotonic sequence $ \varphi $ that selects witnesses for the eventually true property $ P $.
